Cc: ethan@vertexhealth.com
Date: Sat, 19 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: VertexHealth — exploring dedicated capacity for clinical summarization

Hi Olga,

Thanks for taking this — I'm Emma (Head of Platform at VertexHealth). We're evaluating Redwood for a dedicated capacity deployment to power our clinical note summarization and triage assistant. High level: we need a private/reserved pool (HIPAA scope) that can handle a mix of batch and interactive load.

Can you share your pre-sales sizing checklist so we can give you accurate numbers? Quick context so you have a sense of scale:
- Users: ~28k active clinicians, ~3k daily active writers
- Traffic mix: 70% asynchronous batch jobs (end-of-day summarization), 30% interactive (clinician assist)
- Estimated monthly generation tokens: ~1.1 billion tokens
- Typical prompt length: 200–500 tokens (avg ~320)
- Typical response length: 200–800 tokens (avg ~480)
- Peak concurrent interactive sessions (expected): ~450 concurrent at peak day spikes
- Latency target (interactive): p95 < 600ms, p99 < 1.2s (for short prompts)

We have an initial SOC2 report and a HIPAA BA in process — I attached a short list of SLA/security asks (vertex_sla_requirements.pdf).

If you can send the checklist (or the questionnaire your infra team prefers) we'll fill it out and loop in engineering. Happy to do a 30-minute technical call early next week.

Best,
Emma

Emma — thanks for the context and the SLA doc, this is helpful.

Looping in Diego (AE) and Marissa (SE) to own the technical intake. Below is a short intake we use to produce a first-pass footprint and pricing. If you can fill the bullets below and attach a 24–72 hour token-level traffic sample (CSV) we'll run a quick simulation and come back with a starter sizing recommendation.

Key items we need:
- Typical prompt and response token distributions (CSV preferred: timestamp, prompt_tokens, response_tokens, request_type)
- Session model: are interactive sessions long-lived with cache reuse or mostly one-off requests?
- Percent read/write mix and batch window shape (e.g., end-of-day windows)
- SLOs: p50/p95/p99 latency targets for interactive vs. batch
- Model and quality tolerance: do you require a specific model family (e.g., llama/opt/redwood-verified) or are you open to quantized/16-bit variants?
- Data residency / VPC requirements and expected traffic egress patterns
- Expected concurrency profile: baseline vs. peak spike duration (minutes/hours)
- Any hard start/stop windows (e.g., daily midnight batch run)

I'll have Marissa attach our full technical questionnaire (detailed traffic shapes, prompt taxonomy, RLHF/regeneration ratios, caching expectations, etc.). Once you return the completed form + sample we can do a sizing run and propose a starter reserved pool (and optional burst policy).

Next steps:
1) Emma — ideal if you can send a 48hr sample CSV and mark any PII-sensitive columns.
2) Diego — will set up a 30-min technical call for Tue/Wed next week.
3) Marissa — please attach the questionnaire and any sizing templates.

Thanks — Olga

Hi Emma and team — attaching our detailed Dedicated Capacity Intake questionnaire. Below is the condensed version (fill what's available; we can iterate):

1) Traffic and request shape
- Avg prompt tokens (mean, 25/50/75 pctiles)
- Avg response tokens (mean, 25/50/75 pctiles)
- Percentage of requests that include attachments/images (affects KV cache and preprocessing)
- Proportion of requests that are streaming vs. synchronous

2) Concurrency and burst profile
- Baseline interactive concurrency and expected peak (numeric)
- Typical spike duration and recurrence (minutes/hours/daily)
- Batch window cadence and average batch concurrency

3) Session and caching behavior
- Are sessions long-lived? If yes, average session length and average KV reuse per session
- Do prompts share large prefixes (templates) that would benefit from prefix caching?

4) Model & operational constraints
- Target model family / acceptable quantization (int8/4, float16, etc.)
- Required latency SLOs (p50/p95/p99) for interactive and batch jobs
- Throughput priority: minimize cost per token vs. minimize latency

5) Security & deployment
- VPC/Private deployment required? (yes/no)
- KMS/HSM requirements, audit retention, SOC2/HIPAA notes (attach docs)

6) Non-functional
- Maintenance windows, backup SLAs, rollback window tolerance

Please upload a small traffic_sample.csv (timestamp,prompt_tokens,response_tokens,request_type) to the Drive link Olga shared. If you prefer, reply inline with the answers below.

Attachment: redwood_dedicated_sizing_questionnaire.pdf (QUESTIONNAIRE)

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Emma Reyes <emma@vertexhealth.com>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, olga.petrov@redwood.ai
Cc: ethan@vertexhealth.com
Date: Mon, 21 Dec 2026 08:17:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: VertexHealth — exploring dedicated capacity for clinical summarization (answers + sample)

Thanks Marissa — inline answers below, attaching a 48h sample (traffic_sample.csv). I redacted PHI columns per your note.

1) Traffic and request shape
- Avg prompt tokens: mean 330 (p25 180, p50 320, p75 460)
- Avg response tokens: mean 470 (p25 210, p50 450, p75 680)
- Attachments/images: ~6% of requests (mostly imaging references, not raw images)
- Streaming: ~22% interactive requests enable incremental streaming

2) Concurrency and burst profile
- Baseline interactive concurrency: 120
- Peak interactive concurrency: 450 (usually 10–20 minute spikes tied to shift changes)
- Typical spike duration: 10–25 minutes, recurring daily at 07:00 and 19:00 local time
- Batch cadence: nightly batches between 02:00–04:30 with very high token volumes but relaxed latency (p95 batch completion under 30m acceptable)

3) Session and caching behavior
- Sessions: medium-lived (average session 6–12 minutes) with moderate KV reuse for patient context (~30% reuse)
- Prefix reuse: high for templated prompts (orderable discharge template)

4) Model & operational constraints
- Open to mid-sized encoder-decoder or decoder-only families; prefer float16 or int8 quantized variants if latency OK
- Interactive SLOs: p95 < 600ms, p99 < 1.2s (short prompts), batch SLOs: completion within nightly window
- Priority: first minimize latency for interactive, then cost for batch

5) Security & deployment
- Private VPC deployment required; HIPAA BA in place, SOC2 report attached (vertex_sla_requirements.pdf)
- KMS for key management; audit logs retained for 12 months

6) Non-functional
- Maintenance window tolerance: prefer weekends; cannot have large upgrades during nightly batch window

Attached: traffic_sample.csv (CSV, 48h sample, redacted)

Let us know if you need anything else — we can take the technical call Tue morning PST.

—Emma

Subject: Re: VertexHealth — exploring dedicated capacity for clinical summarization (starter footprint & next steps)

Emma — thanks for the fast turnaround and the sample. We ran a first-pass simulation against your 48h sample and the answers you provided. High-level starter recommendation (ballpark, subject to final simulation):

Starter reserved pool (private/VPC):
- Recommended GPU mix: 8 x H100-80GB (or 12 x A100-80GB equivalent) as a starter; tuned for low-latency interactive workloads and nightly batch concurrency.
- Autoscale / burst: add a burst policy to allow short-duration +30% extra capacity for the 10–25 minute spikes (billing on usage).
- Model config: float16 quantized variant for main model; keep a smaller low-latency model as a fallback for extreme spikes.

Operational notes:
- Caching: high prefix reuse you reported gives ~18–24% token cost reduction with prefix caching enabled; we will configure aggressive KV eviction policies tuned to 6–12 minute session lengths.
- Batching: nightly batch runs can be scheduled to use preemptible capacity where permitted to save cost.
- Latency: with the above footprint we expect to meet your p95/p99 interactive targets on typical prompts; we'll validate on a canary.

Attachments: redwood_dedicated_pricing.xlsx (starter pricing by committed capacity), traffic_sample.csv (kept for our sizing run), vertex_sla_requirements.pdf (from your earlier mail).

Next steps:
1) Diego will send a calendar invite for Tue 08:30 PST technical call to review sizing and verify VPC/KMS requirements.
2) We'll run a deeper simulation with a 7-day sample and provide a 2x/3x sizing sensitivity matrix.
3) If the canary looks good, we'd propose a 90-day reserved commit + burst policy for the initial deployment.

If you want, Marissa can prepare a quick cost/latency tradeoff slide to review on the call.

Thanks — looking forward to the call.

—Olga
